status_summary: Executive Order 14149 (signed 2025-01-20, 90 FR 8243) directed the Attorney General, consulting agency heads, to review federal activities of the prior four years that conflicted with its free-speech policy and to report to the President. An Attorney General memorandum of 2025-02-05 created a Weaponization Working Group to review civil and criminal enforcement activity of departments and agencies over the last four years, listing named matters including a 2023 FBI memorandum, with quarterly reports to the White House, and rescinded the 2021 school-board memorandum. The memorandum names no active FBI investigation and does not direct a review of all major active FBI investigations; an undated Working Group report on the 2021 memorandum said most related FBI assessments had been closed or discontinued. On 2026-04-14 the Department released a Working Group report on FACE Act enforcement, with corrective steps; it concerns closed prior enforcement rather than active FBI investigations.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14149 directed the Attorney General, with agency heads, to review federal government activities of the prior four years that conflicted with its free-speech policy and to report findings and recommended remedies to the President.

The Attorney General issued a memorandum establishing a Weaponization Working Group to review enforcement activity across agencies over the prior four years, with named matters, and to send quarterly progress reports to the White House; a footnote rescinded the 2021 school-board threats memorandum.
timeline.source: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of the Attorney General

timeline.event: The Department of Justice released a Weaponization Working Group report on the Biden-era enforcement of the Freedom of Access to Clinic Entrances (FACE) Act, based on a review of over 700,000 internal records, and listed corrective steps including dismissal with prejudice of three civil suits and a directive limiting future abortion-related FACE Act actions to extraordinary circumstances or significant aggravating factors; the release does not mention the FBI.
timeline.source: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs

title: Review active FBI and DOJ investigations and end those deemed unlawful or politicized
uncertainties: The Working Group report prints no date in the text read and refers to a 2026-06-11 roundtable as past, so it is labeled undated and not placed in the timeline. News on FBI personnel changes appeared in research searches but was not opened. The Working Group looks back at prior enforcement across agencies; the memorandum does not direct a review of all active FBI investigations, so the match is partial. The Executive Order text and the 2025-02-05 memorandum were re-read in this pass and match the timeline; the match stays partial because the review is retrospective. The 2026-04-14 report was read through the Department's press release on justice.gov, not the report itself; the release does not say whether it is the Working Group's first report, names no FBI investigation and announces no further reports, and its page metadata shows posting on the evening of 2026-04-13 (Eastern time) under a 2026-04-14 release date. A Federal Register search for the Weaponization Working Group since 2025-02-01 returned no documents. The Working Group's leadership was reported by Lawfare (2026-05-14) to have changed in 2026; this was not verified on a primary source.
